title: How a Ink Stamp Pad Works

facts.intro: A bright red cam sits on a fixed axle, ready to turn as you press the handle.
facts.reveal: When you rotate the cam, its raised lobe contacts the bottom of the plunger.
facts.step1: The plunger is forced upward, pulling the ink‑soaked pad away from the paper.
facts.step2: At the peak of the cam’s lift, the pad is fully exposed and ready for a clean imprint.
facts.step3: Continuing the turn lets the cam’s low side drop, allowing the spring to push the plunger down.
facts.step4: The plunger presses the pad back onto the paper, transferring the ink in a crisp shape.
facts.hold: If you pause at the top, the pad stays lifted, showing the mechanism frozen in action.
facts.payoff: Release the cam and the spring snaps the plunger back, resetting the stamp for the next use.
